approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Otter Tail Power Company South Dakota customer for the installation address and applicable electric service or rate.
Purchase and install new equipment or complete a measure that meets the current program's measure-specific efficiency, sizing, and control requirements.
Obtain advance approval when seeking an Energy Control rebate of $10,000 or more.

Submit the complete signed rebate application by March 31 following the installation year with the account information, itemized receipts, manufacturer and model details, and required AHRI certificates or specifications.
Allow Otter Tail Power Company to review and, when requested, inspect or otherwise verify the completed project before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Otter Tail Power Company currently publishes standard South Dakota rebate forms and measure requirements rather than a competitive selection process. A qualifying, timely, fully documented project is likely to be paid after review and any required verification, subject to program acceptance and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Otter Tail Power Company's current South Dakota application requires qualifying equipment, a complete account-based claim, itemized purchase documentation and technical support, with advance approval for large Energy Control rebates and utility verification before payment.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Otter Tail Power Company Minnesota residential customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying new product or measure that meets the applicable efficiency, sizing, baseline, and service-rate requirements.
Enroll in or maintain the required controlled-service rate when a listed incentive depends on controlled electric service.
Obtain advance approval for an Energy Control rebate of $10,000 or more and any other measure expressly requiring preapproval.

Submit the current signed application by the stated deadline with itemized receipts, equipment information, AHRI certificates or other technical documentation, and permit or contractor information when required.
Allow Otter Tail Power Company to verify the installation or inspect the property when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Minnesota residential program uses published, measure-specific rebate rules and administrative review rather than competitive scoring. Eligible customers that satisfy any controlled-rate or preapproval condition and submit complete documentation are likely to receive the applicable rebate after verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Otter Tail Power Company lists current Minnesota residential efficiency programs and requires a timely application, qualifying equipment, receipts and measure-specific technical records; some incentives also require controlled service, preapproval or inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Owatonna Public Utilities residential customer for the service and measure involved.
Purchase and install a new product or improvement included in the current residential rebate offering.
Meet the minimum efficiency, equipment, installation, and baseline requirements stated on the current measure application.
Submit the current rebate application with the utility account information, paid receipt or invoice, and required equipment or contractor documentation by the applicable deadline.
Permit Owatonna Public Utilities to review and verify the claim or installation when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Owatonna Public Utilities currently lists a broad set of residential efficiency rebates governed by published product and filing rules. A qualifying customer with a complete, timely claim is likely to receive the stated rebate after administrative review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Owatonna Public Utilities residential rebate page lists 2026 appliance, HVAC, heat-pump, thermostat, envelope, EV-charging, and water-saving offers and directs customers to the current applications for efficiency standards and terms.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Owen Electric Cooperative member at the participating residence.
Meet the applicable program's existing-home, primary-heating, equipment-baseline, and efficiency requirements.
For Button-Up improvements, schedule and complete the required pre-improvement assessment or heat-loss calculation before completing the recommended work.
For SimpleSaver, enroll an eligible central air-conditioning system and qualifying thermostat in the demand-response program.
Install qualifying equipment through the applicable contractor or program pathway and provide the requested application, invoices, equipment records, and completion information.
Complete any required post-improvement calculation, inspection, commissioning, or program verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Owen Electric currently offers defined member pathways for heat pumps, weatherization and thermostat-based energy control. These are not competitively ranked, so a member that meets the program-specific baseline and completes the required assessment, enrollment, documentation and verification is likely to receive the applicable benefit.
reviews.evidenceText: Owen Electric's current pages describe heat-pump rebates, pre- and post-improvement Button-Up assessments, and SimpleSaver thermostat enrollment, each with member, equipment and verification conditions.

approvalRequirements: Be an Ozark Border Electric Cooperative member in good standing at a service location using at least 6,000 kilowatt-hours per year.
Install the qualifying new equipment in a permanent structure on land owned by the member.
Meet the current measure-specific equipment, efficiency, sizing, and installation requirements.
Submit a complete rebate application with the member account information and original dated receipt within 90 days of purchase.
Allow the cooperative to conduct a random inspection or other verification of the installation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Ozark Border publishes objective member, equipment, timing and documentation rules for current rebates. A qualifying installation with a complete claim submitted within 90 days is likely to receive the rebate, subject to cost limits and any inspection.
reviews.evidenceText: The current cooperative page requires a member in good standing, minimum annual use, new qualifying equipment, a complete application and original receipt within 90 days, and permits random inspection.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible commercial, industrial, private agricultural, nonprofit, or multifamily property in a Texas jurisdiction that has established a PACE program.
Propose a permanent energy or water improvement, including eligible storage, whose useful life and projected savings satisfy program requirements.
Be current on property taxes and mortgage obligations, have satisfactory title and financial standing, and not be in bankruptcy.
Obtain private-capital financing and written consent from each mortgage holder.
Submit the preliminary and final program materials, including the required technical review and project documentation.
Close the PACE financing and assessment before construction, then complete required post-installation verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Texas PACE provides a defined financing mechanism, but project participation depends on the local jurisdiction, property and owner eligibility, private-lender underwriting, mortgage-holder consent, technical review and successful closing. Eligible technology alone does not assure financing.
reviews.evidenceText: Texas PACE Authority requires an eligible participating-jurisdiction property, qualifying permanent improvements, satisfactory tax and mortgage status, private financing, mortgagee consent, technical review and execution of the PACE assessment before installation.

approvalRequirements: Use an eligible commercial, industrial, nonprofit, or multifamily property with at least five units in a Massachusetts municipality that has opted into PACE Massachusetts.
Propose an eligible energy improvement, including a permanently installed standalone energy-storage system when applicable.
Demonstrate through the required technical review that projected energy savings and project economics satisfy the program standards.
Secure private financing and obtain all required owner, lender, mortgage-holder, municipal, and program consents or approvals.
Submit the complete application and supporting project documents within the applicable permitting or post-completion window.
Receive final program review and close the betterment assessment and financing before relying on PACE funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PACE Massachusetts makes eligible storage and efficiency projects financeable through a structured process, but approval still depends on municipal participation, technical and economic qualification, private capital, lienholder consent and final program closing. Conditional review is not a guaranteed financing commitment.
reviews.evidenceText: MassDevelopment's current PACE materials cover qualifying commercial and multifamily properties in participating municipalities, expressly include permanent standalone energy storage, and require technical review, private financing, consents and final assessment closing.

approvalRequirements: Propose a new or expanded, locally owned, grid-connected renewable-energy project at a nonresidential site served by Pacific Power or Rocky Mountain Power.
Keep the project within the program's technology, ownership, size and service-territory requirements and provide the requested renewable-energy and community-benefit data.
Demonstrate meaningful community engagement and provide the required applicant or third-party cost share, generally 20% to 50% of project cost.
Contact the program manager and submit a complete funding application for committee review before treating the project as funded.
If selected, enroll in Blue Sky as required, execute the award documents, complete the approved project, and provide reporting and recognition materials.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Blue Sky Community Project funding is competitive and limited. A qualifying renewable project may be selected, but award depends on comparative committee review, community value, match funding, program priorities and available funds rather than compliance alone.
reviews.evidenceText: Pacific Power accepts rolling community-project applications, reviews them through a funding committee, requires qualifying locally owned renewable projects and community participation, and states that awards depend on limited available funds and program priorities.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pacific Power California residential customer, property owner, landlord, or other participant under an applicable residential rate schedule.
Purchase and install a currently listed qualifying appliance, heat-pump water heater, thermostat, fan-motor, heat-pump, or other measure that meets the current specifications.
Use a qualifying contractor or installation pathway when the measure rules require one and comply with applicable permits and codes.
Submit the online incentive application through the current program or My Account pathway with the invoice, model and efficiency information, and other required documentation.
Apply within the measure-specific time limit and permit program verification when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Pacific Power currently offers formulaic California residential incentives for specified appliances, water-heating and HVAC measures. A qualifying customer with a timely, complete claim is likely to receive the listed incentive, although the current offer is narrower than the legacy DSIRE retrofit mapping.
reviews.evidenceText: The current California wattsmart site lists residential incentives for qualifying appliances, heat-pump water heaters, thermostats, fan motors and heat pumps and directs eligible customers to an online claim process with measure-specific requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pacific Power Washington residential customer, property owner or landlord under an applicable residential rate schedule.
Install a currently qualifying heat pump, duct-sealing measure, insulation improvement, or other listed measure meeting the baseline and technical specifications.
Use an approved or appropriately licensed contractor or direct-install pathway when required by the measure rules.
Submit the current online claim with the invoice, equipment or insulation details, contractor information and other required supporting records.
Allow any required program inspection, diagnostic testing or verification and comply with current incentive caps and available-funding rules.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Washington residential program publishes measure-specific heat-pump, duct and weatherization incentives rather than competitively ranking claims. A qualifying installation submitted through the required contractor or claim pathway is likely to receive the incentive after verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Pacific Power's current Washington wattsmart pages list heat-pump, duct-sealing and insulation incentives with customer, rate-schedule, contractor, baseline, documentation and verification conditions.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pacific Power California nonresidential customer at the project site.
Select equipment or a custom project that meets the current wattsmart Business eligibility, efficiency and savings requirements.
For most lighting and custom projects, obtain the required preinspection, written approval or incentive offer before ordering equipment or beginning work.
For listed measures that permit post-purchase filing, retain the required invoices, specifications and installation records and submit the application within the current deadline.
Provide the application, W-9, invoices, product data and requested cost or savings documentation and pass any required post-installation inspection or verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: California wattsmart Business uses published prescriptive and custom review pathways rather than competitive award ranking. Once required advance approval is secured for lighting or custom work, a compliant completed project is likely to receive the approved incentive after final documentation and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Pacific Power's current California business materials distinguish post-purchase listed incentives from lighting and custom projects that require advance review, and require final applications, cost records and inspection or verification before payment.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pacific Power Washington nonresidential customer at the project site.
Use qualifying equipment or a custom project that meets the current wattsmart Business specifications and energy-savings requirements.
For lighting and custom projects, complete the required preinspection and obtain written authorization or a signed incentive offer before purchasing equipment or starting work.
For listed measures eligible for post-purchase filing, submit the application and supporting documentation within the applicable period.
Provide the W-9, invoices, product data, cost and savings records, and other requested documents and pass final inspection or verification before incentive payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Washington wattsmart Business program follows objective prescriptive or approved custom pathways. A qualifying customer that observes the advance-authorization rule for lighting or custom work and passes final review is likely to receive the applicable incentive, subject to program terms and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Pacific Power's 2026 Washington business materials require advance authorization for lighting and custom projects, permit post-purchase claims for specified listed measures, and condition payment on complete documentation and final verification.

approvalRequirements: Be a Palmetto Electric Cooperative member installing a qualifying geothermal ground-source heat-pump system at the member's property.
Use a properly licensed contractor and install the system in compliance with applicable utility requirements, permits and codes.
Complete the rebate form with the contractor and submit it before installation.
Notify the cooperative when installation is complete and provide the requested equipment, contractor and project documentation.
Pass Palmetto Electric's final inspection or verification before the rebate is issued.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Buried Treasure offering is a prescriptive geothermal rebate, not a competitive grant. A member installing a qualifying ground-source system is likely to receive the rebate after timely preinstallation filing and successful final inspection; the current page does not substantiate a general air-source HVAC rebate under this program.
reviews.evidenceText: Palmetto Electric currently offers a per-ton ground-source heat-pump rebate and requires a member-contractor application before installation, code-compliant work, completion notice and final cooperative inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Parke County REMC member at the installation address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying heat pump, geothermal system, heat-pump water heater, thermostat or other covered measure.
Meet the current efficiency, sizing, installation and baseline requirements and obtain AHRI certification or load calculations when required.
Submit the completed rebate application within 120 days of purchase or installation with the itemized paid invoice and required technical documentation.
Allow Parke County REMC or the Power Moves program to inspect or otherwise verify the installation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Parke County REMC publishes current, measure-specific bill-credit rebates with a defined 120-day filing process. A member with qualifying equipment, complete technical support and a verifiable installation is likely to receive the applicable credit.
reviews.evidenceText: The current cooperative page lists heat-pump, geothermal, water-heating and thermostat incentives and requires a timely application, paid invoice, AHRI or sizing documents when applicable, and access for inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualified person or business engaged in agricultural production or harvesting under California's partial farm-equipment exemption rules.
Purchase qualifying solar-power equipment or components specifically designed to provide power to eligible farm machinery or other qualifying agricultural equipment.
Use the solar system at least 50% of the time in qualifying agricultural production or harvesting activities and substantiate the use allocation.
Provide the seller a timely, properly completed partial-exemption certificate at the time of purchase or through the permitted correction process.
Retain system, purchase and electricity-use records, including the first 12 months of annual-use support when required, for CDTFA review or audit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: This is a statutory partial sales-and-use-tax exemption rather than a discretionary award. A qualified agricultural buyer that purchases eligible solar property, meets the use test and supplies a valid exemption certificate should receive the reduced tax treatment, subject to later audit or adjustment.
reviews.evidenceText: Current CDTFA guidance applies a partial tax exemption to qualifying farm equipment and may cover solar systems designed to power eligible agricultural machinery when the qualified-person, 50% use, exemption-certificate and recordkeeping requirements are met.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pasadena Water and Power commercial, workplace, multifamily, fleet or other nonresidential electric customer at the charger site.
Select a new qualifying Level 2 or DC fast charger and comply with the applicable networking, power, site and incentive-category requirements.
Submit the commercial charger application and building or electrical permit information before project completion to reserve program funds.
Install the charger in compliance with code, obtain the required permit signoff and utility or city inspection, and remain within site and customer caps.
Before the reservation expires, submit the signed agreement, paid invoices or receipts, inspection signoff and other final documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Pasadena Water and Power currently offers formulaic per-port commercial charger rebates through a reservation-and-redemption process. A qualifying project that reserves funds before completion and passes permit, documentation and inspection review is likely to receive the rebate, subject to caps and remaining funds.
reviews.evidenceText: PWP's current commercial charger page requires an application and permit information before completion, then paid documentation and inspection signoff before the reservation deadline; published rebates vary by charger type and eligible site category.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an active Pasadena Water and Power commercial electric account in good standing at the project site.
Purchase and install equipment that meets the current listed-measure specifications or propose a qualifying customized energy-savings project.
For a customized project, submit the application and savings estimate, complete the preinspection, and receive a written reservation before purchasing equipment or starting work.

For a listed business rebate, submit the claim after installation with the detailed paid invoice, specification sheet, installation photographs, W-9 and any required permit or nameplate documentation.
Complete the project within the applicable reservation period and pass final program review or inspection while remaining within cost, account and fiscal-year caps.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PWP's current listed rebates are administrative claims, and its customized incentives use a defined reservation and inspection process rather than competitive ranking. A compliant customer is likely to receive the applicable rebate after satisfying the correct pathway, documentation, cap and verification rules.
reviews.evidenceText: PWP currently requires active commercial service, qualifying equipment and paid project documentation for listed rebates; customized projects require advance reservation, preinspection, completion within six months and final invoice and inspection review.

approvalRequirements: Be an active Pasadena Water and Power residential electric customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a new qualifying wall-mounted Level 2 charger meeting the current certification, connector, networking and equipment requirements.
Use a licensed contractor when required, obtain the electrical permit, comply with local codes and pass final permit inspection.
Apply after installation and within 180 days of purchase using the online residential EV rebate process.
Upload the itemized paid receipt or invoice, charger and installation photographs, permit signoff and other requested account or equipment documentation, and allow onsite verification if selected.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PWP's residential charger rebate uses published equipment and documentation rules rather than competitive selection. An active customer with a qualifying permitted installation and a complete claim filed within 180 days is likely to receive the stated rebate after review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current PWP residential EV page offers rebates for qualifying Level 2 chargers and requires active service, eligible new equipment, permitted code-compliant installation, filing within 180 days, paid documentation, photographs and inspection records.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pasadena Water and Power residential customer at the property receiving the qualifying utility service.
Purchase and install a measure currently included in PWP's residential savings, electrification, water-conservation, EV, solar or battery offerings and meet its measure-specific specifications.
Use a qualifying contractor and obtain permits or inspections when required for the selected equipment or installation.

Submit the claim through the current PWP account or program pathway by the measure-specific deadline with paid invoices, model and efficiency information, photographs and other required documentation.
Comply with current household, property, quantity and cost caps and allow program review or inspection.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PWP maintains active, measure-specific residential rebate and assistance pathways rather than a single competitive award pool. A customer whose selected measure is currently covered and whose claim is timely, complete and verifiable is likely to receive the applicable benefit.
reviews.evidenceText: PWP's current residential savings pages list appliance, heating and cooling, thermostat, insulation, water, electrification, EV, solar and battery programs and route customers to measure-specific claims and account-based applications.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Tennessee small business, commercial or industrial enterprise, private nonprofit, or other borrower served by Pathway Lending's sustainability financing.
Propose an eligible energy or sustainability project with an acceptable scope, budget, contractor or vendor plan, and intended energy or operating benefits.
Complete Pathway Lending's loan inquiry and application process and provide the requested borrower, ownership, financial and project documentation.
Pass credit, repayment-capacity, collateral and other lender underwriting requirements.
Accept the approved terms and execute the loan and project documents before funds are disbursed or committed to the work.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Pathway Lending currently offers sustainability loans for eligible Tennessee projects, but financing is subject to borrower-specific credit approval and negotiated loan terms. An eligible retrofit does not by itself assure approval or funding.
reviews.evidenceText: Pathway Lending's current sustainability page advertises low-interest financing for Tennessee efficiency and renewable projects, while its lending materials state that loans remain subject to credit approval and underwriting.

approvalRequirements: Use a residence served by Pearl River Valley Electric Power Association through the required qualifying meter and electric-service arrangement.
For a new home, meet the published Comfort Advantage envelope, window, air-sealing, electric heat-pump, sizing and efficiency standards.
For an existing home, install a qualifying heat pump in a home that is not already a Comfort Advantage home.
Provide any contractor, equipment, construction or verification information requested by the cooperative.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current official help page states Comfort Advantage standards and incentive amounts, but it does not provide a current application, filing deadline, approval sequence, inspection process or funding status. Award likelihood cannot be determined without current program-administration evidence.
reviews.evidenceText: Pearl River Valley Electric Power Association's official page describes new- and existing-home heat-pump incentives and detailed building standards, but it does not expose a current claim or approval procedure sufficient to estimate award likelihood.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible nonresidential PECO electric customer at the proposed charging location.
Install new qualifying networked Level 2 charging ports or an eligible public-benefit charging project, including qualifying charging equipment, installation or make-ready work.
Submit the first-stage rebate reservation before ground-breaking or incurring project costs and receive a reservation while annual funds remain available.
Complete and energize a Level 2 project within 270 days of reservation, or an eligible DC fast-charging project within the longer 450-day period.
Submit the redemption documentation showing the completed, operational installation and comply with the required network communications and two years of charging-data reporting.
Remain within the applicable per-port, project, customer and annual program caps.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PECO's EVsmart commercial charging program is currently extended through May 31, 2029 and uses a reservation-and-redemption process with published incentive amounts. A technically eligible project that reserves funds before costs are incurred and completes all installation and data requirements is likely to receive the reserved rebate, subject to the annual budget and caps.
reviews.evidenceText: Current program materials describe Level 2 and public-benefit charging rebates, a two-stage preconstruction reservation and postinstallation redemption process, completion deadlines, annual caps, networked-data requirements and program operation through May 31, 2029.

approvalRequirements: Be a PECO residential or business customer eligible for the current Smart Driver rebate.
Purchase a qualifying electric vehicle and notify PECO through the current online application pathway.
Provide the customer, account, vehicle-purchase and other documentation required by the current terms and conditions.
Recognize that the published $50 benefit is tied to the purchased electric vehicle and does not reimburse EV-charger installation under this program.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PECO currently offers $50 per car for reporting an electric-vehicle purchase, but the official program does not substantiate reimbursement for the mapped EV-charger installation. A charger project therefore is unlikely to receive an award through this specific opportunity, even though the separate vehicle-notification rebate remains available.
reviews.evidenceText: PECO's current Smart Driver page states that residential and business customers can earn $50 per car by notifying PECO of an electric-vehicle purchase; it does not identify charger equipment or installation as an eligible cost under this rebate.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible PECO commercial or nonresidential electric customer at the project location.
Purchase and install qualifying equipment or complete an eligible custom project under the current Phase V business-incentive rules.

Use an instant-discount distributor when that pathway applies, or submit a complete incentive application with the PECO bill, scope or estimate, equipment specifications, calculator or savings support, W-9 and authorization documents.
Complete any preinstallation review or verification requested by the program; preapproval is recommended but is not a universal requirement for every measure.
After installation, submit the final invoice and payment request, commissioning or completion records, and any other required documents and pass final verification.
Apply while first-come program funds remain available and within all measure and project caps.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PECO's Phase V business program, effective June 1, 2026, uses published equipment, custom and instant-discount pathways rather than competitive ranking. A qualifying project with complete documentation and successful verification is likely to receive the incentive while first-come funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: PECO's current business program covers equipment and custom efficiency projects through instant discounts or documented applications, may conduct pre- and post-verification, processes complete claims first-come, and identifies Phase V as running from June 1, 2026 through May 31, 2031 unless funds end earlier.

approvalRequirements: Be a PECO residential electric or natural-gas customer, as applicable to the measure, at the residence where the qualifying equipment is installed.
Purchase and install a new product that meets the current ENERGY STAR, unit-efficiency and measure-specific eligibility requirements.
For equipment purchased or installed on or after June 1, 2026, ensure the application is received within 90 days of purchase or installation.
Submit the claim online, through an eligible contractor, or by the permitted paper pathway with a paid receipt showing the model number, manufacturer, price and purchase date.
Avoid claiming a second rebate when an instant discount or another excluded incentive has already been applied and allow program verification when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PECO's Home Rebates program is currently extended through 2031 and uses objective product, service, filing and documentation rules. A qualifying customer whose complete claim is received within 90 days is likely to receive the listed rebate after administrative review.
reviews.evidenceText: Current PECO Home Rebates materials state that the program is extended through 2031 and require new qualifying equipment, PECO residential service, a claim within 90 days for purchases or installations on or after June 1, 2026, and a paid receipt with model, manufacturer, price and date.
